The Model GTP305-2 APU is a single shaft, all shaft power engine with an axial-centrifugal compressor, reverse flow annular combustor, and radial-axial turbine.
The APU was designed to produce 186.3 shaft horsepower, 171.0 horsepower/ft^3, and 1.86 horsepower/lb at a design speed of 76,585 rpm and turbine rotor inlet temperature of 2050°F.
The high-pressure compressor flow was increased by 10% to improve matching with the low-pressure compressor.
The combustion system features a reverse flow annular combustor with an air-assist/airblast fuel injection system and a ceramic coated sheet metal design.
The combustion system goals were to achieve an average combustor discharge temperature of 2067°F, a temperature spread factor of 0.15, and a combustor liner pressure drop of 5.0%.
The fatigue life of the radial turbine rotor was improved through the use of hot isostatic pressing (HIP) to close casting micro-shrinkage.

The integrated components assembly (ICA) testing showed that the design efficiency goals for the turbine were exceeded, and the combustor demonstrated a temperature spread factor of 0.163 and a pressure drop of 4.9% at design conditions.
The final rotating group design had critical speeds of 37,000 rpm, 57,000 rpm, and 77,000 rpm.
The cold air turbine testing was conducted to evaluate the aerodynamic performance of the radial and axial turbine components, as well as the effects of cooling flow on turbine efficiency.
The radial turbine nozzle was designed with cooling fins and a scalloped backface to improve efficiency.
The axial turbine stator and rotor were designed using a non-free vortex approach to optimize efficiency.
The turbine exhaust diffuser was designed with 5 constant cross-section struts to minimize pressure losses.
The radial turbine rotor was cast from the AF2-1DA alloy, which was selected for its high-temperature strength and creep resistance.
The combustion system development testing included evaluating different fuel injection configurations and cooling schemes to improve performance and durability.
The integrated components assembly (ICA) testing was conducted to validate the overall performance of the APU at the design operating conditions.
